system.name: Brain-tuning
system.one_liner: Fine-tunes pretrained speech language models on fMRI recordings of people listening to stories to raise brain alignment and semantic downstream performance.

content.variant_note: (a) is a left-to-right network strip; (b) adds the evaluation pipeline and (c) an expected-outcome table, so the figure runs method, measurement, expectation
content.argues: Fine-tuning a speech model on fMRI responses should raise alignment with semantic brain regions, lower the impact of low-level features on that alignment and improve downstream semantic tasks.
content.subject: a speech model fine-tuned to predict fMRI, the pipeline that measures brain alignment and low-level impact, and an expected-outcome grid

lessons.what_to_learn: Pair the training network with an expected-outcome table that has the same model icon as row heads, colour-scale column heads and up or down Better arrows, so the hypothesis is drawn before any result. Snowflake and flame icons with Freeze and Fine-tune captions state the trained parts at a glance.
lessons.suits: Fine-tuning papers that must show a method, how it is measured and what success would look like, especially when the metrics point in different directions.

summary: The paper proposes brain-tuning: fine-tuning pretrained speech language models on fMRI recordings of people listening to stories so they gain brain-relevant semantics. Figure 1 has three parts. Panel (a) draws the training network as one left-to-right strip: audio passes a frozen Feature Extractor (snowflake) and fine-tuned Transformer Layers (flame), output tokens are pooled and projected by an FC layer to a predicted fMRI response, which meets the voxel-masked true response in a loss. Panel (b) shows how brain alignment and low-level feature impact are estimated from original and residual representations. Panel (c) is a pretrained versus brain-tuned table over brain alignment, low-level impact and downstream tasks, drawn with brain-surface maps, bars, colour scales and Better arrows.
summary_zh: 论文提出脑调优：用听故事时的 fMRI 数据微调语音模型。图 1 分三部分：(a) 冻结特征提取器、微调 Transformer 并回归 fMRI 的训练网络；(b) 估计脑对齐与低层特征影响；(c) 预训练与脑调优的预期对比。
notes: The prior pass counted two panels; the figure has three (a), (b), (c). Only the (a) caption is inside the figure; the (b) caption is cut off in the preview and the (c) caption is not visible, so their labels come from the figure caption in the context file. The brain maps and bars in (c) are described as expected outcomes in the caption, so they are recorded as illustrations, not results.
